CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..error: Thinks the lesson is only about money.

example.question: What does the parable of the talents teach a Grade 5 learner?
example.wrong_answer: Keep your money safe and never spend it
example.correct_answer: Use the gifts and abilities God has given you

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..cause: A talent in the story was a large sum of money, so the child reads the story as advice about savings.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..reveals: Offer "Keep your money safe and never spend it" beside "Use the gifts and abilities God has given you" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..help: Ask what the servants did with what they were given. Then name other gifts: singing, kindness, farming, drawing, helping.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..feedback: In the story a talent was a sum of money, but Jesus told it to teach us to use every gift and ability God gives us, not only money.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..error: Thinks the master was unfair, or that the third servant was punished for having least.

example.question: Why was the third servant blamed?
example.wrong_answer: He was given less than the others
example.correct_answer: He buried his talent and did not use it

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..cause: The child notices the amounts (five, two, one) and thinks that having less is the fault.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..reveals: Offer "He was given less than the others" beside "He buried his talent and did not use it" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..help: Reread Matthew 25:15, "each according to his ability", then the servant's own words about fear and the buried talent.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..feedback: The master gave each servant a share to match his ability. The third servant was blamed because he buried his talent and did not use it, not because he was given less.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..error: Mixes up the numbers of talents given and gained.

example.question: How many talents did the first servant gain?
example.correct_answer: Five more

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..cause: The child remembers five, two and one but not which servant gained what.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..reveals: Offer "Two more" beside "Five more" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..help: Draw three columns: given, gained, total. Fill them from Matthew 25:16-18.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..feedback: The servant who was given five talents gained five more, the one given two gained two more, and the one given one buried it and gained nothing.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..error: Thinks gifts are given so that a person can be admired or win.

example.question: According to 1 Peter 4:10, what should each person do with the gift received?
example.wrong_answer: Show it off so others admire you
example.correct_answer: Use it to serve others

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..cause: Children see talent shows and prizes and link gifts to winning.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..reveals: Offer "Show it off so others admire you" beside "Use it to serve others" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..help: Read 1 Peter 4:10 aloud and ask who benefits when a gift is used to serve.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..feedback: 1 Peter 4:10 says each person should use the gift received to serve others, as a good steward of God's grace. A gift is for service, not for showing off.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..error: Thinks God has a purpose only for adults or only for people with big talents.

example.question: What does Jeremiah 29:11 say about God's plans?
example.wrong_answer: God has plans only for adults
example.correct_answer: God has plans for welfare, a future and hope

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..cause: The child thinks purpose belongs to jobs and grown-ups.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..reveals: Offer "God has plans only for adults" beside "God has plans for welfare, a future and hope" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..help: Read Jeremiah 29:11 and ask who God is speaking about. Say that a Grade 5 child is included.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..feedback: Jeremiah 29:11 says that God has plans for our welfare, to give us a future and a hope. A child is part of that, not only an adult.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..error: Thinks a person's abilities come only from the person's own effort.

example.question: According to James 1:17, where does every good gift come from?
example.wrong_answer: From a person's own hard work alone
example.correct_answer: From God, the Father of lights

CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..cause: Effort is praised at school, so the giver is forgotten.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..reveals: Offer "From a person's own hard work alone" beside "From God, the Father of lights" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..help: Read James 1:17. Say that work matters, but that the ability to work and learn is a gift too.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..feedback: James 1:17 says that every good and perfect gift comes from above, from God. Hard work matters, but the abilities we work with are gifts too.
CRES.G5.CREATI.MY_PURPOSE_TALENTS_AND_A..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_RU.error: Reads "rule over" in Genesis 1:26 as permission to use up or harm creation.

example.question: What does it mean to rule over the animals and plants in Genesis 1:26 and 2:15?
example.wrong_answer: Use them as we like, even if they are finished
example.correct_answer: Look after them as God's caretaker

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_RU.cause: The word rule is heard as power, not as care.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_RU.reveals: Offer "Use them as we like, even if they are finished" beside "Look after them as God's caretaker" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_RU.help: Read Genesis 2:15 beside it: "to work it and take care of it".
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_RU.feedback: Genesis 2:15 shows what ruling means: to work the garden and take care of it. Human beings are God's caretakers of creation, not owners who may use it up.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_RU.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_WO.error: Thinks work is only a punishment.

example.question: When did God first give human beings work in the Bible?
example.wrong_answer: After they did wrong, as a punishment
example.correct_answer: In the garden, before they did wrong

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_WO.cause: Work is hard at times, so the child thinks it began as a punishment.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_WO.reveals: Offer "After they did wrong, as a punishment" beside "In the garden, before they did wrong" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_WO.help: Compare Genesis 2:15 (work in the garden) with Genesis 3.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_WO.feedback: In Genesis 2:15 God put the man in the garden to work it and take care of it before anything went wrong. Work is a good gift and a responsibility.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_WO.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_HO.error: Thinks a child has a role only at home.

example.question: Which one is a role a child can do at church?
example.correct_answer: Helping to keep the church compound clean

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_HO.cause: The child lists chores for home and misses school and church roles.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_HO.reveals: Offer "Cleaning the compound at home" beside "Helping to keep the church compound clean" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_HO.help: Make three lists on the board: home, school and church.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_HO.feedback: A child has roles at home, school and church. At church a child can sing, help as an usher, sweep, and help keep the compound clean.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.STEWARDSHIP.M_STW_HO.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CH.error: Thinks every chore at home is child labour.

example.question: Which of these is child labour?
example.correct_answer: Carrying heavy loads for hours instead of going to school

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CH.cause: The child hears that work for children is wrong and applies it to every chore.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CH.reveals: Offer "Sweeping the room after school" beside "Carrying heavy loads for hours instead of going to school" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CH.help: Sort tasks by three questions: is it safe, does it suit my age, does it stop me from school or rest?
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CH.feedback: Light chores that suit your age, such as sweeping or washing dishes, are good training. Child labour is work that is harmful or takes a child away from school, rest and play.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CH.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_LA.error: Thinks child labour is good because it teaches a child to work or earns money.

example.question: What is a common effect of child labour?
example.wrong_answer: The child learns more at school
example.correct_answer: The child misses school and can be hurt

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_LA.cause: The child links any work with growing up well.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_LA.reveals: Offer "The child learns more at school" beside "The child misses school and can be hurt" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_LA.help: Name a child who herds all day and cannot read. Ask what the child lost.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_LA.feedback: Child labour takes children from school and can harm their health and safety. Learning to work happens through safe chores, not through harmful work.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_LA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_RE.error: Thinks a child forced to work should tell the employer or keep quiet.

example.question: Whom should a child tell if he is forced to work?
example.correct_answer: A trusted adult such as a teacher, the chief or a parent

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_RE.cause: The child fears the person in charge.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_RE.reveals: Offer "The person who forces him" beside "A trusted adult such as a teacher, the chief or a parent" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_RE.help: Make a list of safe adults together, including the Childline Kenya line 116.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_RE.feedback: A child who is forced to work should tell a trusted adult such as a parent, a teacher or the chief, or call the Childline Kenya helpline on 116. Not the person who is forcing the work.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_RE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CA.error: Blames the child or says children work only because they are lazy at school.

example.question: What is one cause of child labour in many places?
example.wrong_answer: Children who like to be lazy
example.correct_answer: Poverty in the family

CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CA.cause: The child blames the child instead of the conditions.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CA.reveals: Offer "Children who like to be lazy" beside "Poverty in the family" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CA.help: Ask what a family with no food might feel it must do.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CA.feedback: Child labour is often caused by poverty, the loss of parents, ignorance of children's rights and the greed of those who use cheap labour. It is not the fault of the child.
CRES.G5.CREATI.WORK.CHILD_LABOUR.M_CL_CA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.error: Says the fruit was an apple.

example.question: What does Genesis 3 say about the kind of fruit that was eaten?
example.correct_answer: The Bible does not name the fruit

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.cause: Pictures and stories name the fruit, and the child remembers the picture.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.reveals: Offer "It was an apple" beside "The Bible does not name the fruit" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.help: Read Genesis 3:6 and look for the name of the fruit together.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.feedback: Genesis 3 says "the fruit of the tree" but does not name it. The apple comes from pictures and stories, not from the Bible.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.error: Thinks only one person ate or that the other was not involved.

example.question: Who ate the fruit God had forbidden?
example.correct_answer: The woman, who then gave some to her husband, and he ate

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.cause: The child remembers the woman and the serpent but not the man.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.reveals: Offer "Only the woman" beside "The woman, who then gave some to her husband, and he ate" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.help: Read Genesis 3:6 and count who ate.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.feedback: In Genesis 3:6 the woman ate the fruit and she also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate. Both disobeyed God.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.error: Thinks the serpent told the truth or was a friend.

example.question: What did the serpent do?
example.wrong_answer: He told them the truth about God
example.correct_answer: He tempted them to doubt what God said

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.cause: The child follows the serpent's smooth words in the story.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.reveals: Offer "He told them the truth about God" beside "He tempted them to doubt what God said" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.help: Compare what God said in Genesis 2:17 with what the serpent said in 3:4.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.feedback: The serpent made the woman doubt what God had said. He tempted them, and what he said was not true.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.error: Thinks blaming someone else is an acceptable answer to wrong done.

example.question: After eating the fruit, the man blamed the woman. What should a person do when he does wrong?
example.correct_answer: Admit it honestly and say sorry

CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.cause: The child sees blame as a way out, as the man did.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.reveals: Offer "Blame someone else" beside "Admit it honestly and say sorry" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.help: Read Genesis 3:12-13 and ask whether blaming helped.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.feedback: Adam blamed Eve and Eve blamed the serpent. Blaming others does not remove our own wrong. A person should admit what he did and say sorry.
CRES.G5.CREATI.THE_FALL_OF_MAN.FALL_OF_M.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.error: Thinks a united family never disagrees.

example.question: What is family unity?
example.correct_answer: Living together in love, helping and forgiving one another

CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.cause: The child sees unity as the absence of noise.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.reveals: Offer "Never disagreeing about anything" beside "Living together in love, helping and forgiving one another" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.help: Read Colossians 3:13-14: bear with each other and forgive. That assumes there are things to forgive.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.feedback: A united family has disagreements too, but its members forgive each other and keep loving one another (Colossians 3:13-14).
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.error: Thinks only parents are responsible for a happy family.

example.question: Who can help to make a family happy?
example.correct_answer: Every member of the family, including children

CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.cause: The child thinks children only receive.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.reveals: Offer "Only the parents" beside "Every member of the family, including children" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.help: List three things a child can do: chores, kind words, obedience.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.feedback: Every member of the family, including children, can help to make a family happy by obeying, doing chores and speaking kindly.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.error: Thinks forgiving means pretending nothing happened or that wrong was right.

example.question: What does it mean to forgive a family member?
example.wrong_answer: To pretend nothing wrong was done
example.correct_answer: To let go of the anger and choose to love again

CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.cause: The child mixes forgiving with ignoring.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.reveals: Offer "To pretend nothing wrong was done" beside "To let go of the anger and choose to love again" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.help: Say what Colossians 3:13 asks: forgive as the Lord forgave you.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.feedback: To forgive is to let go of anger and choose to love again. It does not pretend that nothing was wrong.
CRES.G5.CREATI.FAMILY_UNITY.FAMILY_UNITY.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.error: Thinks the Bible is useful only inside church.

example.question: Where does the Bible guide a Christian?
example.correct_answer: At home, school, church and in the community every day

CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.cause: The child meets the Bible mostly in church.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.reveals: Offer "Only at church on Sunday" beside "At home, school, church and in the community every day" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.help: Ask for a verse that helps at home or at school.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.feedback: The Bible guides a Christian in every place and every day: at home, at school, at church and in the community.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.error: Thinks reading the Bible once is enough.

example.question: What does Joshua 1:8 ask about God's word?
example.wrong_answer: Read it once and then keep it safe
example.correct_answer: Think about it day and night and do what it says

CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.cause: The child thinks of reading as finishing a book.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.reveals: Offer "Read it once and then keep it safe" beside "Think about it day and night and do what it says" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.help: Read Joshua 1:8 and Psalm 1:2, "his delight is in the law of the Lord".
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.feedback: Joshua 1:8 asks us to think on God's word day and night and to do what it says. It is for daily use, not for reading once.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.error: Does not know what Psalm 1:1-3 compares the person who loves God's word to.

example.question: In Psalm 1:3, the person who delights in God's word is like...
example.correct_answer: A tree planted by streams of water

CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.cause: The child remembers an image from the Bible but not which.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.reveals: Offer "A strong wall" beside "A tree planted by streams of water" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.help: Read Psalm 1:3 and draw the tree.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.feedback: Psalm 1:3 says that the person who delights in the word of the Lord is like a tree planted by streams of water, which gives fruit in its season.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.THE_BIBLE_AS_A_GUIDE.BIBL.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..error: Mixes this story with Peter denying Jesus and thinks Peter was afraid to speak.

example.question: How did Peter speak to the rulers in Acts 4?
example.wrong_answer: He was afraid and said he did not know Jesus
example.correct_answer: He spoke boldly, filled with the Holy Spirit

CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..cause: The child remembers Peter's denial in the courtyard.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..reveals: Offer "He was afraid and said he did not know Jesus" beside "He spoke boldly, filled with the Holy Spirit" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..help: Read Acts 4:8 and 4:13: "filled with the Holy Spirit", "the courage of Peter and John".
CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..feedback: In Acts 4 Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit and spoke boldly. That is different from the night when he denied Jesus.
CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.THE_BI.BIBLE_STORIES_PETER_AND_..error: Thinks Peter and John promised to stop speaking about Jesus.

example.question: What did Peter say about salvation in Acts 4:12?
example.wrong_answer: That there are many ways and names
example.correct_answer: That there is no salvation in any other name than Jesus

CRES.G5.THE_LI.THE_BAPTISM_OF_JESUS_CHR..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.error: Thinks the early believers kept their possessions private.

example.question: What did the early believers do with what they owned?
example.correct_answer: Shared it with anyone in need

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.cause: The child compares with life today.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.reveals: Offer "Kept it for themselves" beside "Shared it with anyone in need" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.feedback: They shared what they had with anyone who was in need. They were united in giving and helping.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.error: Thinks unity means everyone doing the same thing.

example.question: What keeps a church united?
example.wrong_answer: Everyone doing exactly the same job
example.correct_answer: Love, sharing, forgiveness and humility

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.cause: The child confuses unity with sameness.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.reveals: Offer "Everyone doing exactly the same job" beside "Love, sharing, forgiveness and humility" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.help: List values and ask which can be practised by anyone.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.feedback: A church is united by love, sharing, forgiveness and humility. People may do different things and still be one.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.error: Gets the list of things the believers devoted themselves to wrong.

example.question: Which one did the early believers devote themselves to?
example.correct_answer: The apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread and prayer

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.cause: The child skips the list in verse 42.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.reveals: Offer "Selling things for profit" beside "The apostles' teaching, fellowship, breaking bread and prayer" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.help: Read Acts 2:42 and write the four things.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.feedback: Acts 2:42 says that they devoted themselves to the apostles' teaching, to fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayers.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_EARLY_CHURCH.EARLY_CH.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.error: Thinks only one name for the Lord's Supper is correct.

example.question: Churches call the Lord's Supper by different names. Which is true?
example.wrong_answer: Only one name is correct and the others are wrong
example.correct_answer: Lord's Supper, Lord's Table, Holy Communion and Eucharist are names used for the same remembrance

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.cause: The child hears one name at home.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.reveals: Offer "Only one name is correct and the others are wrong" beside "Lord's Supper, Lord's Table, Holy Communion and Eucharist are names used for the same remembrance" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.help: Ask your own church's name and the names other churches use.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.feedback: Different churches use different names such as Lord's Supper, Lord's Table, Holy Communion or Eucharist for the same remembrance of Jesus. The children in a class may know different names.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.source: to confirm by a CRE teacher who knows the school's tradition

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.error: Mixes the time or the people at the supper.

example.question: With whom did Jesus share the Passover meal in Luke 22?
example.wrong_answer: With a crowd of five thousand
example.correct_answer: With his apostles

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.cause: The child mixes this with a feeding miracle.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.reveals: Offer "With a crowd of five thousand" beside "With his apostles" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.feedback: Jesus sat at the table with his apostles at the Passover meal.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.error: Thinks the meal is a normal meal or a reward for good behaviour.

example.question: What did Jesus say to do with the bread and the cup?
example.wrong_answer: Do this as a prize for the best behaved
example.correct_answer: Do this in remembrance of me

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.cause: The child does not link it to remembering.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.reveals: Offer "Do this as a prize for the best behaved" beside "Do this in remembrance of me" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.feedback: Jesus said, "Do this in remembrance of me." Christians remember what Jesus did for them whenever they share the bread and the cup.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_LORD_S_SUPPER.LORDS_S.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.error: Mixes the gifts and the fruit of the Spirit.

example.question: Which one is a fruit of the Holy Spirit?
example.correct_answer: Kindness

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.cause: Both lists have nine items and sound alike.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.reveals: Offer "Prophecy" beside "Kindness" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.help: Make two lists, gifts from 1 Corinthians 12 and fruit from Galatians 5.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.feedback: Kindness is one of the fruit of the Spirit (Galatians 5:22-23). Prophecy is one of the gifts (1 Corinthians 12:10).
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.error: Gets the number of gifts or fruit wrong.

example.question: How many gifts of the Holy Spirit are listed in 1 Corinthians 12:1-11?
example.correct_answer: Nine

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.cause: The child remembers a number but not which.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.reveals: Offer "Five" beside "Nine" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.help: Count the gifts in verses 8 to 10 together.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.feedback: 1 Corinthians 12:8-10 lists nine gifts of the Spirit: wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, telling spirits apart, tongues, and interpreting tongues.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.error: Does not see how the fruit help people live together.

example.question: How does the fruit of patience help Christians?
example.wrong_answer: It makes them leave quarrels unsolved
example.correct_answer: It helps them to bear with one another and live in harmony

CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.cause: The child sees the fruit as private feelings.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.reveals: Offer "It makes them leave quarrels unsolved" beside "It helps them to bear with one another and live in harmony" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.help: Ask what a patient friend does when you make a mistake.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.feedback: Patience, kindness, gentleness and self-control help Christians to bear with one another and live in harmony.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.THE_HOLY_SPIRIT.HOLY_SPIR.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..error: Thinks Peter broke out of prison by his own effort.

example.question: How did Peter get out of prison?
example.correct_answer: An angel woke him and the chains fell off

CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..cause: The child likes an escape story.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..reveals: Offer "He broke the chains himself" beside "An angel woke him and the chains fell off" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..feedback: An angel of the Lord appeared, woke Peter, and the chains fell off his hands. The gates opened by themselves.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..error: Thinks the church was not praying, or forgot Peter.

example.question: What was the church doing while Peter was in prison?
example.correct_answer: Praying earnestly to God for him

CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..cause: The child focuses on Peter alone.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..reveals: Offer "Waiting quietly and doing nothing" beside "Praying earnestly to God for him" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..feedback: The church was earnestly praying to God for Peter while he was in prison.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..error: Thinks Rhoda opened the gate at once.

example.question: What did Rhoda do when she heard Peter's voice?
example.correct_answer: Ran in with joy and forgot to open it

CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..cause: The child skips the funny detail.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..reveals: Offer "Opened the gate immediately" beside "Ran in with joy and forgot to open it" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..feedback: Rhoda was so glad that she ran in to tell the others without opening the gate. They did not believe her at first.
CRES.G5.THE_CH.PETER_S_MIRACULOUS_RESCU..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.error: Chooses friends by popularity or what they own.

example.question: Which is the best reason to choose a friend?
example.wrong_answer: Because he is popular and has nice things
example.correct_answer: Because he is honest, kind and respectful

CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.cause: The child looks at what others admire.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.reveals: Offer "Because he is popular and has nice things" beside "Because he is honest, kind and respectful" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.help: List qualities with the class before naming friends.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.feedback: A good friend is chosen for good character: honest, kind, respectful and responsible. Popularity and possessions are not the test.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.error: Thinks you must do what a friend asks to keep the friendship.

example.question: A friend asks you to copy answers in a test. What should you do?
example.wrong_answer: Copy so that you keep your friend
example.correct_answer: Say no politely and offer to help study instead

CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.cause: The child fears losing the friend.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.reveals: Offer "Copy so that you keep your friend" beside "Say no politely and offer to help study instead" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.help: Practise a short polite refusal in pairs.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.feedback: A good friend does not push you to do wrong. You can say no politely. A real friend will respect that.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.error: Does not know what Proverbs 22:24-25 warns about.

example.question: What does Proverbs 22:24-25 advise?
example.wrong_answer: Be friends with a person who has a quick temper
example.correct_answer: Do not make friends with a person who is easily angered

CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.reveals: Offer "Be friends with a person who has a quick temper" beside "Do not make friends with a person who is easily angered" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.feedback: Proverbs 22:24-25 says that you should not make friends with a person who has a hot temper, or you may learn his ways.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.FRIENDSHIP_FORMATION.FRIE.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.error: Thinks changes of growing up are shameful and must be hidden.

example.question: How should a child feel about the changes of adolescence?
example.correct_answer: They are normal, and I can ask a parent or trusted adult

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.cause: The child hears no open talk at home.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.reveals: Offer "Ashamed, and tell no one" beside "They are normal, and I can ask a parent or trusted adult" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.help: Say that all adults went through the same changes.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.feedback: The changes of growing up are normal. A child can ask a parent, guardian, teacher or trusted adult for the right information.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.error: Trusts friends or the internet as the best source about the body.

example.question: Where is the best place to find the right information about growing up?
example.wrong_answer: From friends and anything on the internet
example.correct_answer: From a parent, guardian, teacher or health worker you trust

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.cause: The child asks those the same age.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.reveals: Offer "From friends and anything on the internet" beside "From a parent, guardian, teacher or health worker you trust" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.help: Compare a friend's guess with a nurse's answer.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.feedback: Friends and the internet can give wrong or harmful information. The right information comes from a parent, guardian, teacher or health worker you trust.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.error: Thinks a secret friendship with an older person is harmless.

example.question: Which is a sign of an unhealthy friendship?
example.wrong_answer: The friend says to keep it secret and gives gifts for favours
example.correct_answer: The friend respects you and your parents know about it

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.reveals: Offer "The friend says to keep it secret and gives gifts for favours" beside "The friend respects you and your parents know about it" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.help: List warning signs: secrecy, pressure, gifts for favours.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.feedback: Secrecy, pressure and gifts for favours are warning signs of an unhealthy relationship. A child should tell a trusted adult at once.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.error: Mixes up the changes in boys and girls.

example.question: Which change usually happens in girls at adolescence?
example.correct_answer: Monthly periods begin

CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.cause: The child has heard fragments from friends.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.reveals: Offer "The voice becomes deep" beside "Monthly periods begin" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.feedback: Monthly periods begin in girls and the voice deepens in boys. Both grow taller and grow body hair. These are normal changes.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.HUMAN_SEXUALITY.ADOLESCEN.source: The learner reads the passage loosely or mixes it with a similar Bible story (to confirm by a CRE teacher)

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.error: Thinks sanctity of life means only that we must not kill animals.

example.question: What does it mean that human life is sacred?
example.wrong_answer: Human life is holy because it comes from God and is made in his image
example.correct_answer: Animals must never be used

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.cause: The child extends the word sacred.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.reveals: Offer "Human life is holy because it comes from God and is made in his image" beside "Animals must never be used" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.feedback: Human life is sacred because God gave it and made us in his image (Genesis 1:27). We are not to take human life (Genesis 9:6).
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.error: Thinks that the best way to cope with anger is to hit back.

example.question: What is a safe way to cope with anger?
example.wrong_answer: Hit back so that the other child learns
example.correct_answer: Walk away, breathe, and tell a trusted person

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.cause: The child sees revenge as justice.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.reveals: Offer "Hit back so that the other child learns" beside "Walk away, breathe, and tell a trusted person" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.feedback: Hitting back can cause harm. A safe way to cope with anger is to walk away, calm down, and talk to a trusted person or pray.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.error: Thinks life comes from parents alone or from chance.

example.question: According to Christian teaching, who is the source of life?
example.correct_answer: God, the giver of life

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.cause: The child sees parents as the source.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.reveals: Offer "Only a person's parents" beside "God, the giver of life" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.feedback: Parents bring a child into the world, but God is the source and giver of all life.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SANCTITY_OF_LIFE.SANCTITY.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks medicine from a hospital is the same as drug abuse.

example.question: Which is drug abuse?
example.wrong_answer: Taking medicine as the doctor says
example.correct_answer: Sniffing glue to feel different

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The child hears drug and thinks of anything swallowed.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Taking medicine as the doctor says" beside "Sniffing glue to feel different" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Ask the difference between medicine given by a nurse and a pill taken for fun.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Medicine taken as a health worker directs is not drug abuse. Drug abuse is using a substance such as alcohol, bhang or glue in a way that harms the body and mind.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks only adults abuse alcohol and drugs, or that a child cannot be tempted.

example.question: Who can be tempted to use drugs?
example.correct_answer: Both adults and children, especially when friends pressure them

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The child sees drug use in adults only.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Only adults" beside "Both adults and children, especially when friends pressure them" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Ask about older pupils who offer cigarettes.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Children can be tempted too, often by friends or by wanting to feel grown up. It is important to know the dangers and how to say no.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks trying a drug once will do no harm.

example.question: What is true about trying a harmful drug just once?
example.wrong_answer: One try can never harm you
example.correct_answer: It can start a habit that is hard to break

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "One try can never harm you" beside "It can start a habit that is hard to break" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..help: Say that many people started with one try.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Even one try can start a habit that is hard to stop. Proverbs 20:1 warns that strong drink leads people astray.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..error: Thinks drugs make a person stronger or better at school.

example.question: What is an effect of alcohol and drug abuse?
example.correct_answer: Poor health, failing at school and quarrels

CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..cause: The child hears claims of strength and relief.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..reveals: Offer "Better health and better marks" beside "Poor health, failing at school and quarrels" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..feedback: Alcohol and drug abuse harm the body and the mind and lead to failing at school, quarrels, crime and addiction.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.ALCOHOL_DRUGS_AND_SUBSTA..source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.error: Thinks it is safe to share passwords, address and photos with online friends.

example.question: Which information must you keep private online?
example.correct_answer: Your password and home address

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.cause: The child treats online friends like real friends.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.reveals: Offer "Your favourite colour" beside "Your password and home address" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.help: List what a stranger could do with an address.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.feedback: Never share your passwords or home address online. They can be used to hurt you or take over your account.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.error: Thinks social media has only advantages, or only disadvantages.

example.question: What is a disadvantage of social media?
example.wrong_answer: It helps you talk to relatives far away
example.correct_answer: It can waste time and spread false or harmful messages

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.cause: The child hears one side only.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.reveals: Offer "It helps you talk to relatives far away" beside "It can waste time and spread false or harmful messages" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.help: Make two lists, advantages and disadvantages.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.feedback: Social media has advantages, such as contacting relatives and learning, and disadvantages, such as wasted time, unkind messages and false news.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.error: Thinks a stranger who is kind online can be trusted and met.

example.question: A stranger online says he is a child and asks to meet you. What should you do?
example.wrong_answer: Meet him, because he is kind
example.correct_answer: Do not reply, and tell a parent or teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.cause: The child cannot tell who is really online.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.reveals: Offer "Meet him, because he is kind" beside "Do not reply, and tell a parent or teacher" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.help: Say that people can lie about who they are.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.feedback: People online may not be who they say. Never agree to meet a stranger from the internet. Tell a parent or trusted adult.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.error: Thinks forwarding any message, even if unkind or unproven, is harmless.

example.question: You receive an unkind message about a classmate. What should you do?
example.correct_answer: Delete it and not pass it on

CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.cause: The child sees forwarding as a click.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.reveals: Offer "Forward it to the class" beside "Delete it and not pass it on" and ask the child to choose.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.help: Ask how the classmate would feel.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.feedback: Forwarding an unkind or unproven message can hurt a person. A person with integrity does not pass it on.
CRES.G5.CHRIST.SOCIAL_MEDIA.SOCIAL_MEDIA.source: common learner error; to confirm by a CRE teacher
